Moves a compute target into a different compartment. When provided, If-Match is checked against ETag values of the resource. 
[Command Reference](changeComputeTargetCompartment)

params.help: The [OCID] of the compute target. [required]

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the compartment where the resource should be moved. [required]

params.name: if_match
params.help: For optimistic concurrency control. In the PUT or DELETE call for a resource, set the `if-match` parameter to the value of the etag from a previous GET or POST response for that resource. The resource is updated or deleted only if the `etag` you provide matches the resource's current `etag` value.

params.name: compartment_id
params.help: The [OCID] of the compartment where you want to create the compute target. [required]

 [required]

params.name: display_name
params.help: A user-friendly display name for the resource.

params.name: description
params.help: A short description of the compute target.

params.name: metadata
params.help:
Metadata for the compute target. The size of metadata must be less than 2048 bytes. Key should be under 32 characters. Key should contain only letters, digits and underscore (_) Key should start with a letter. Key should have at least 2 characters. Key should not end with underscore eg. `TEST_` Key if added cannot be empty. Value can be empty. No specific size limits on individual Values. But overall metadata is limited to 2048 bytes. Key can't be reserved Compute Target metadata.
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: freeform_tags
params.help:
Free-form tags for this resource. Each tag is a simple key-value pair with no predefined name, type, or namespace. See [Resource Tags]. Example: `{"Department": "Finance"}`
This is a complex type whose value must be valid JSON. The value can be provided as a string on the command line or passed in as a file using
the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: defined_tags
params.help:

the file://path/to/file syntax.

The --generate-param-json-input option can be used to generate an example of the JSON which must be provided. We recommend storing this example
in a file, modifying it as needed and then passing it back in via the file:// syntax.

params.name: wait_for_state
params.help: This operation asynchronously creates, modifies or deletes a resource and uses a work request to track the progress of the operation. Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the work request reaches a certain state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACCEPTED --wait-for-state CANCELED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the work request to reach the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the work request has reached the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.

params.help:

Example: `50`

params.name: page
params.help:
For list pagination. The value of the `opc-next-page` response header from the previous "List" call.

See [List Pagination].

params.name: sort_order
params.help: Specifies sort order to use, either `ASC` (ascending) or `DESC` (descending).

params.name: sort_by
params.help: Specifies the field to sort by. Accepts only one field. By default, when you sort by `timeCreated`, the results are shown in descending order. When you sort by `displayName`, the results are shown in ascending order. Sort order for the `displayName` field is case sensitive.

params.name: all_pages
params.help: Fetches all pages of results. If you provide this option, then you cannot provide the --limit option.

params.name: page_size
params.help: When fetching results, the number of results to fetch per call. Only valid when used with --all or --limit, and ignored otherwise.

Specify this option to perform the action and then wait until the work request reaches a certain state. Multiple states can be specified, returning on the first state. For example, --wait-for-state ACCEPTED --wait-for-state CANCELED would return on whichever lifecycle state is reached first. If timeout is reached, a return code of 2 is returned. For any other error, a return code of 1 is returned.

params.name: max_wait_seconds
params.help: The maximum time to wait for the work request to reach the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 1200 seconds.

params.name: wait_interval_seconds
params.help: Check every --wait-interval-seconds to see whether the work request has reached the state defined by --wait-for-state. Defaults to 30 seconds.
